newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's imports off 5.6 pct in 1st half 1996.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's imports off 5.6 pct in 1st half 1996.

text.p: The value of Venezuela's imports fell by $280 million, or 5.6 percent, in the first six months of 1996 to $4.712 billion, compared to 4.992 billion in the same period of 1995, according to the Central Office of Statistics and Information (OCEI).
Imports in the month of July, at $935 million, were down $173 million, or 15.6 percent from $1.108 billion in July 1995, the OCEI said in a release.
An overvalued currency saw imports in Venezuela rise 45 percent to $11.156 billion last year.
The private sector accounted for the vast majority of imports in the first six months of 1996 with 85 percent of the total.
"Electrical materials" was the biggest category of imports with 27.8 percent of the total. "Chemical Products" followed with 14.9 percent, then "Common Metals" with 11.6 percent.

The United States was the top exporter to Venezuela with 43.5 percent, followed by Colombia with 10.2 percent, Germany with 5.5 percent, Brazil with 4.9 percent, Japan with 3.0 percent and Italy with 2.6 percent.
